task.title: TestMeasureCommandTerminatesTimedOutDescendant flakes under full-suite load
task.description:
internal/perf's TestMeasureCommandTerminatesTimedOutDescendant (command_test.go ~87) fails with "helper recorded no usable pid" when the whole tree runs under load: seen 2026-10-01 during four concurrent suites and again 2026-10-07 inside scripts/cut-release.sh's own go test ./... (the perf package took 199 s that run). It passes 5/5 alone and 10/10 under eight CPU burners, so plain CPU contention is not enough; the reproduction needs fork-heavy neighbors such as internal/cli's tests.

Mechanism, from reading proctest.go: MeasureCommand gets Timeout 100 ms. Inside that window the leader shell (BusyLeaderArgs) has to fork a second sh (startDescendant), which writes its own pid to the file, and the leader busy-waits for the file. When fork latency under contention exceeds 100 ms, the timeout kills the process group before the pid file exists, and RequireDescendantTerminated fatals on the missing pid rather than on anything the product did. The product behavior (kill the group on timeout) is fine; the test's clock starts before its own fixture is ready.

Fix: make the fixture independent of the timeout. Either have the test wait for the pid file itself before the measured timeout can matter (for example start the measured command with a generous timeout and only assert TimedOut once the pid is recorded, or split pid-recording out of the measured command), or raise the 100 ms budget to something a loaded laptop cannot miss (one or two seconds; the test asserts only TimedOut and descendant termination, so the test gets slower by that much and nothing else changes). Prefer the first. Prove it with the fork-heavy reproduction (perf test -count=40 while go test ./internal/cli runs) before and after.


Reproduction attempts on 2026-10-07, all green: 5/5 alone; 10/10 under eight `yes` CPU burners; 40/40 while `go test ./internal/cli` ran alongside. The failure needs the whole tree in flight (load average 6-7 and the perf package itself stretched to 199 s), so reproduce with the full `go test ./...` and `-count` on the perf package rather than a synthetic load, and treat a fix that cannot be shown to bite as unproven.
